taxonomyNote: NatureServe's standard name is 'Razor-backed Musk Turtle' with 'Keeled Musk Turtle' and 'Razorback Musk Turtle' as alternates.
fieldMarks: Small turtle, carapace about 10-12 cm; high, triangular, domed shell with a prominent medial keel; scutes light brown to orange with dark streaks that fade with age.
Yellowish plastron that is reduced and weakly hinged, with ten rather than eleven scutes (no gular scute).
Skin gray to pink to light brown with small dark spots; slightly hooked jaws with dark streaks, pair of chin barbels and a tubular snout.
Males have longer, thicker tails and rough scale patches on the thighs.
behavior: Diurnal, active mornings and late afternoons; spends more time basking high on deadwood than other musk turtles.
Hibernates underwater; active roughly March-November in Oklahoma and largely crepuscular in summer.
Omnivorous bottom feeder on insects, crustaceans, mollusks (including invasive Asian clams), amphibian larvae, carrion and aquatic plants.
habitat: Medium to large flowing streams and rivers, also swamps and lakes, with soft or sandy/rocky bottoms, aquatic vegetation and basking deadwood.
range: South-central United States: Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma and Texas (Brazos River in Texas to the Pascagoula River in Mississippi); not in Canada.
